title: Load Balancing Neurons: Firing-Rate Control Sustains Plasticity in Continual Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.32691v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Neural networks in continual learning often lose plasticity: some neurons become inactive, while others fire almost constantly. This limits adaptation to shifting data and wastes capacity. Prior work mitigates this by periodically reinitializing low-utility units, but such resets can destroy previously learned features and do not proactively prevent low utility. We study a simple diagnostic measure: the firing rate of ReLU units, defined as the fraction of positive pre-activations. Low rates identify dead units, while very high rates indicate linearized, always-on units. Based on this view, we introduce a lightweight load-balancing mechanism that adjusts per-neuron thresholds to keep firing rates within a target range. Across continual ImageNet and class-incremental CIFAR-100, firing-rate distributions explain differences in plasticity across a range of approaches, including well-known techniques such as L2 regularization and non-affine

translated_title: 负载均衡神经元：激活率控制维持持续学习中的可塑性
translated_abstract: 持续学习中的神经网络常常失去可塑性：一些神经元变得不活跃，而另一些神经元则几乎持续激活。这限制了对变化数据的适应能力，并浪费了网络容量。先前的工作通过定期重新初始化低效用单元来缓解这一问题，但这种重置可能会破坏之前学到的特征，且无法主动预防低效用问题的出现。我们研究了一种简单的诊断指标：ReLU单元的激活率，其定义为正预激活所占的比例。低激活率可以识别出“死亡”单元，而极高的激活率则表明单元已被线性化、始终处于开启状态。基于这一视角，我们引入了一种轻量级的负载均衡机制，通过调整每个神经元的阈值，将激活率保持在目标范围内。在持续ImageNet和类增量CIFAR-100实验中，激活率分布解释了包括L2正则化和非仿射（non-affine）等知名方法在内的一系列方法之间可塑性差异的原因。
tldr: 本文提出一种通过调整每个神经元的阈值来控制ReLU激活率的轻量级负载均衡机制，主动防止神经元死亡或过度激活，从而在持续学习中维持网络的可塑性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a lightweight load-balancing mechanism that adjusts per-neuron thresholds to keep ReLU firing rates within a target range, proactively preventing dead or over-active neurons and thus sustaining plasticity in continual learning.
